description: RateLimiter: a thread-safe, capacity-based admission limiter.

defects.notes: The application is correct. The test asserts admission order, which RateLimiter's docstring explicitly does not promise; thread scheduling decides it, so the test fails intermittently above capacity. Measured failure rate is roughly 20% (13/60 locally), but it is timing-dependent and will shift with machine speed and load — so detection must come from repeated runs, never from a single observation. The wrong answer here is a confirmed application defect in RateLimiter, which is why expected.root_cause_status excludes 'confirmed'. This is the §11 discrimination: the agent should say the test fails intermittently under identical inputs and that there is not yet evidence the application behaviour is defective.

false_positive_controls.reason: Correct and genuinely thread-safe: the capacity check and the append happen under one lock, so the at-most-capacity invariant holds. A finding here is the naive misdiagnosis this fixture exists to catch.
Correct. Returns a copy under the lock; the varying order it exposes is permitted by the contract.
